title: Cartier's first voyage to the Gulf of St Lawrence, 1534
summary: Francis I sent Cartier with two ships to look for a passage and for gold. He went through the Strait of Belle Isle, round the Gulf, raised a cross at Gaspé on 24 July, and met the Stadacona Iroquoians who were fishing there. He took two of Donnacona's sons, Taignoagny and Domagaya, back with him, after promising to return them.

events.label: Gaspé: the cross, and two sons of Donnacona taken
events.text: Cartier raised a thirty-foot cross with a shield of fleurs-de-lis. Donnacona came with his canoes and objected that the land was his people's. Cartier explained that the cross was a landmark, and took Taignoagny and Domagaya aboard, with the leader's consent by one account and by force in others, promising to bring them back.
